claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by T cell proliferation assays and autoimmunity phenotypes.

claims.claim: Pre-positive selection CD4+CD8+ double-positive (DP) CD3−CD69− thymocytes have maximal GFP expression in Rag2p-GFP mice.
claims.source: In pre-positive selection CD4+CD8+ double-positive (DP) CD3−CD69− thymocytes, the Rag2 promoter is active, resulting in maximal GFP expression (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: After receiving a TCR signal, thymocytes upregulate CD3 and CD69, generating early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ cells.
claims.source: After receiving a TCR signal, thymocytes upregulate CD3 and CD69 (Fu et al., 2009), generating early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ cells; the brief time elapsed after positive selection is indicated by continued high GFP expression by this subset (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1B and a citation.

claims.claim: DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes represent post-positive selection thymocytes, as opposed to cells undergoing strong TCR signaling driving clonal deletion.
claims.source: To further evaluate if DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes represent post-positive selection thymocytes, as opposed to cells undergoing strong TCR signaling driving clonal deletion, we evaluated thymocyte subsets from Nr4a1GFP mice, in which GFP levels reflect the strength of TCR signaling (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Moran et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Nr4a1GFP expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: GFP levels in DP CD3loCD69+ cells were substantially lower than in CD25+ CD4SPs, which are mostly Tregs.
claims.source: GFP levels were substantially lower in DP CD3loCD69+ cells than in CD25+ CD4SPs, which are mostly Tregs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: DP CD3+CD69+ cells are MHC-I restricted and have persisted for an intermediate time between CD4SP SM and CD8SP M1 cells after positive selection.
claims.source: Together, these data demonstrate that DP CD3+CD69+ cells are MHC-I restricted and have persisted for an intermediate time between CD4SP SM and CD8SP M1 cells after positive selection, consistent with a co-receptor reversing DP subset.
claims.evidence: This is supported by GFP expression data and analysis in B2m-/- and MHCII-/- mice.

claims.claim: DP CD3+CD69+ cells were significantly reduced in B2m−/− mice, in which positive selection of CD8SP thymocytes is abrogated.
claims.source: Consistent with this possibility, DP CD3+CD69+ cells were significantly reduced in B2m−/− mice, in which positive selection of CD8SP thymocytes is abrogated, as is selection of innate iNKT cells and CD8αα+ IELps (Bendelac et al., 1994; Ruscher et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C and citations.

claims.claim: DP CD3+CD69+ cells were enriched in MHCII−/− mice in which only MHC-I-restricted thymocytes are positively selected.
claims.source: Furthermore, DP CD3+CD69+ cells were enriched in mice with a deletion spanning the MHC-II genes H2-Aa, H2-Eb1, and H2-Eb2 (MHCII−/−) in which only MHC-I-restricted thymocytes are positively selected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

claims.claim: CCR4 is upregulated by the majority of early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes, which do not yet express CCR7.
claims.source: CCR4 is upregulated by the majority of early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes, which do not yet express CCR7 (Figure 1C, D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: CCR7 is expressed at high levels by ~40% CD4SP SM cells, and CCR4 expression persists on this subset.
claims.source: CCR7 is subsequently expressed at high levels by ~40% CD4SP SM cells, and CCR4 expression persists on this subset (Figure 1C, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C, D.

claims.claim: Low-level expression of CCR7 can be detected on additional Ccr7+/+ CD4SP SM cells, consistent with initial upregulation of CCR7 by this subset.
claims.source: In comparison to Ccr7−/− cells, low-level expression of CCR7 can be detected on additional Ccr7+/+ CD4SP SM cells, consistent with initial upregulation of CCR7 by this subset (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data comparing WT and Ccr7-/- cells in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: As thymocytes mature through CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 stages, CCR4 is progressively downregulated.
claims.source: As thymocytes mature through CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 stages, CCR4 is progressively downregulated.
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C, D.

claims.claim: CCR7 expression peaks in both CD4SP and CD8SP M1 subsets and is diminished in M2 cells.
claims.source: CCR7 expression peaks in both CD4SP and CD8SP M1 subsets and is diminished in M2 cells (Figure 1C, D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: Increased expression of cell-surface CCR7 or CCR4 was not detected with increasing incubation time at 37°C.
claims.source: Thymocytes were incubated at 37°C for up to 2 hr, to allow re-expression of internalized receptors, before immunostaining with anti-CCR7 and anti-CCR4 antibodies. Increased expression of cell-surface CCR7 or CCR4 was not detected with increasing incubation time (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, D.

claims.claim: DP CD3loCD69+ cells underwent chemotaxis in response to the CCR4 ligand CCL22, but not the CCR7 ligands CCL19 or CCL21.
claims.source: DP CD3loCD69+ cells, which express CCR4 but not CCR7, underwent chemotaxis in response to the CCR4 ligand CCL22, but not the CCR7 ligands CCL19 or CCL21 (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2.

claims.claim: CCL22-induced chemotaxis occurred in all post-positive selection thymocytes except the most mature M2 thymocyte subsets.
claims.source: CCL22-induced chemotaxis of all subsequent post-positive selection thymocytes, except the most mature M2 thymocyte subsets (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), largely in keeping with CCR4 expression patterns.
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: CCR7-mediated chemotaxis of CD4SP SM and DP CD3+CD69+ subsets did not reach statistical significance when compared to all thymocyte subsets.
claims.source: Although CD4SP SM and DP CD3+CD69+ subsets expressed CCR7 (Figure 1C), CCR7-mediated chemotaxis of these subsets did not reach statistical significance when compared to all thymocyte subsets (Figure 2C, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2C, D.

claims.claim: Moderate CCR7-mediated chemotaxis of CD4SP SM and DP CD3+CD69+ subsets was revealed when considered separately.
claims.source: However, when considered separately, moderate CCR7-mediated chemotaxis of these subsets was revealed, although DP CD3loCD69+ cells still did not undergo CCR7-mediated chemotaxis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The CCR7 ligands CCL19 and CCL21 induced highly efficient chemotaxis of mature CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 subsets.
claims.source: Consistent with expression of CCR7 by more mature thymocyte subsets, the CCR7 ligands CCL19 and CCL21 induced highly efficient chemotaxis of mature CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 subsets (Figure 2C, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2C, D.

claims.claim: All post-positive selection subsets except CD4SP SM and DP CD3+ CD69+ cells underwent chemotaxis to CXCL12.
claims.source: CXCR4 expression decreased after positive selection, but all post-positive selection subsets continued to express CXCR4 (Figure 3A, B), and all except for CD4SP SM and DP CD3+CD69+ subsets underwent chemotaxis in response to CXCL12 (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes are responsive to CCR4 but not CCR7 ligands, with low responsiveness to CXCR4 ligands.
claims.source: Taken together, chemotaxis assays show that early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes are responsive to CCR4 but not CCR7 ligands, with low responsiveness to CXCR4 ligands.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the chemotaxis data from Figures 2 and 3.

claims.claim: CD4SP SM cells undergo chemotaxis toward CCR4 ligands, begin to migrate at a low level toward CCR7 ligands, but not to CXCR4 ligands.
claims.source: At the next stage, CD4SP SM cells also undergo chemotaxis toward CCR4 ligands, and begin to migrate at a low level toward CCR7 ligands, but not to CXCR4 ligands.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the chemotaxis data from Figures 2 and 3.

claims.claim: As thymocytes mature to the CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 stages, they progressively gain the ability to respond robustly to CCR7 ligands, regain CXCR4 responsiveness, and lose responsiveness to CCR4 ligands.
claims.source: As thymocytes mature to the CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 stages, they progressively gain the ability to respond robustly to CCR7 ligands, regain CXCR4 responsiveness, and lose responsiveness to CCR4 ligands (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the chemotaxis data from Figures 2 and 3, illustrated in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: CD4SP SM cells responded efficiently to CCR4 ligands.
claims.source: However, these cells responded efficiently to CCR4 ligands (Figure 2B), and they underwent chemotaxis to the CCR9 ligand CCL25 at levels comparable to DP CD3loCD69+ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), consistent with a previous study showing CCL25 induces migration of most thymocyte subsets (Campbell et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, and a citation.

claims.claim: CD4SP SM cells underwent chemotaxis to the CCR9 ligand CCL25 at levels comparable to DP CD3loCD69+ cells.
claims.source: However, these cells responded efficiently to CCR4 ligands (Figure 2B), and they underwent chemotaxis to the CCR9 ligand CCL25 at levels comparable to DP CD3loCD69+ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), consistent with a previous study showing CCL25 induces migration of most thymocyte subsets (Campbell et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transwell chemotaxis assay data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and a citation.

claims.claim: CCL21a establishes a chemokine gradient that drives accumulation of CD4SP thymocytes in the medulla.
claims.source: CCL21a establishes a chemokine gradient that drives accumulation of CD4SP thymocytes in the medulla (Kozai et al., 2017; Ueno et al., 2002; Ueno et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: CCL22 is expressed predominantly in the medulla.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence analysis revealed that CCL22 is expressed predominantly in the medulla (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), consistent with a potential role in inducing medullary entry of early post-positive selection thymocytes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: OT-II+ Rag2−/− MHCII−/− thymocytes did not express CCR4 or CCR7 due to lack of positive selection in the absence of MHC-II expression.
claims.source: OT-II+ Rag2−/− MHCII−/− mice served as a source of pre-positive selection DP thymocytes that did not yet express CCR4 or CCR7 due to lack of positive selection in the absence of MHC-II expression (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: OT-II+ Rag2−/− MHCII−/− DP cells upregulated CCR4 as early as 3 hr after being introduced onto positively selecting thymic slices.
claims.source: OT-II+ Rag2−/− MHCII−/− DP cells upregulated CCR4 as early as 3 hr after being introduced onto positively selecting thymic slices (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from thymic slice assays in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The frequency of CCR4+ OT-II+ Rag2−/− MHCII−/− cells continued to increase over 24 hr on WT slices.
claims.source: The frequency of CCR4+ cells continued to increase over 24 hr on WT slices.
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from thymic slice assays in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Positive selection was required for initiation of CCR4 expression, as demonstrated by the failure to upregulate CCR4 on non-selecting MHCII−/− slices.
claims.source: Positive selection was required for initiation of CCR4 expression, as demonstrated by the failure to upregulate CCR4 on non-selecting MHCII−/− slices.
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from thymic slice assays in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: CCR7 was not upregulated within 24 hr of initiating positive selection in OT-II+ Rag2−/− MHCII−/− cells.
claims.source: CCR7 was not upregulated within 24 hr of initiating positive selection (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from thymic slice assays in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: OT-II+ thymocytes entered the medulla by 9–12 hr after positive selection.
claims.source: By 9–12 hr after positive selection, OT-II+ thymocytes entered the medulla, as evidenced by a significant increase in medullary density (Figure 4D, E; Video 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 4D, E and Video 2.

claims.claim: CCR4 likely drives medullary entry of early post-positive selection thymocytes.
claims.source: As CCR7 is not yet expressed by these cells (Figure 4C), CCR4 likely drives medullary entry of early post-positive selection thymocytes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of CCR4 upregulation and medullary entry, and the absence of CCR7 expression.

claims.claim: About 10% of OT-I+ Rag2−/− DP cells from β2m−/− hosts expressed CCR4 at baseline.
claims.source: Although OT-I positive selection was largely inhibited in these bone marrow chimeras, about 10% of the DP cells expressed CCR4 at baseline (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B.

claims.claim: CCR4 was upregulated in OT-I+ Rag2−/− cells as early as 3 hr after initiating positive selection in WT thymic slices, but not in non-selecting β2m−/− slices.
claims.source: Nonetheless, CCR4 was upregulated as early as 3 hr after initiating positive selection in WT thymic slices, but not in non-selecting β2m−/− slices and increased over 24 hr (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from thymic slice assays in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B.

claims.claim: CCR7 was not expressed during the first 24 hr after initiation of positive selection in OT-I+ Rag2−/− cells and only became detectable as CD8SP cells differentiated at the 72 hr time point.
claims.source: CCR7 was not expressed during the first 24 hr after initiation of positive selection and only became detectable as CD8SP cells differentiated at the 72 hr time point (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C), consistent with prior observations (Lutes et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from thymic slice assays in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C and a citation.

claims.claim: The medullary density of OT-I thymocytes increased significantly by 12 hr after the initiation of positive selection.
claims.source: Furthermore, two-photon imaging of pre-selection OT-I+ Rag2−/− thymocytes within the cortex and medulla of thymic slices showed that despite medullary entry of some thymocytes at 1.5 hr (Video 3), likely due to the observed baseline CCR4 expression in this model, the medullary density of OT-I thymocytes increased significantly by 12 hr after the initiation of positive selection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E; Video 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E and Videos 3 and 4.

claims.claim: Both MHC-I- and MHC-II-restricted thymocytes upregulate CCR4 within a few hours of the initiation of positive selection and accumulate significantly in the medulla by 9–12 hr.
claims.source: Together, these findings show that both MHC-I- and MHC-II-restricted thymocytes upregulate CCR4 within a few hours of the initiation of positive selection and accumulate significantly in the medulla by 9–12 hr.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the synchronized positive selection assays for both OT-I and OT-II cells.

claims.claim: Thymocyte medullary entry precedes CCR7 upregulation, which does not occur until 48–72 hr after positive selection.
claims.source: Thymocyte medullary entry precedes CCR7 upregulation, which does not occur until 48–72 hr after positive selection.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the synchronized positive selection assays.

claims.claim: The kinetics of CCR4 upregulation are consistent with a role for CCR4 in promoting early medullary entry of positively selected thymocytes.
claims.source: The kinetics of CCR4 upregulation are consistent with a role for CCR4 in promoting early medullary entry of positively selected thymocytes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal correlation between CCR4 upregulation and medullary entry.

claims.claim: Purified WT DP CD3loCD69+ cells entered and migrated within the medulla, accumulating at a twofold higher density than in the cortex.
claims.source: Purified WT DP CD3loCD69+ cells entered and migrated within the medulla, accumulating at a twofold higher density than in the cortex (Figure 5A, B; Video 5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 5A, B and Video 5.

claims.claim: Medullary enrichment of DP CD3loCD69+ cells was abolished when the cells were purified from Ccr4−/− or DKO mice, but Ccr7 deficiency did not diminish their medullary accumulation.
claims.source: Medullary enrichment of this subset was abolished when the cells were purified from Ccr4−/− or DKO mice, but Ccr7 deficiency did not diminish their medullary accumulation (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Paired analyses of WT versus Ccr4−/− and Ccr7−/− versus DKO DP CD3loCD69+ cells imaged together in the same slices confirmed that Ccr4 deficiency significantly impaired medullary accumulation of this early post-positive selection DP subset irrespective of Ccr7 genotype.
claims.source: Paired analyses of WT versus Ccr4−/− and Ccr7−/− versus DKO DP CD3loCD69+ cells imaged together in the same slices confirmed that Ccr4 deficiency significantly impaired medullary accumulation of this early post-positive selection DP subset irrespective of Ccr7 genotype, but genetic deficiency of Ccr7 at this stage did not alter medullary accumulation (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by paired analysis of two-photon imaging data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: CCR4 is required for the twofold accumulation of DP CD3loCD69+ cells in the medulla relative to the cortex.
claims.source: Altogether, CCR4 is required for the twofold accumulation of DP CD3loCD69+ cells in the medulla relative to the cortex.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the imaging data showing loss of medullary enrichment in Ccr4-/- cells.

claims.claim: Accumulation of CD4SP SM cells within the medulla remained at a twofold medullary: cortical density ratio, comparable to that of DPCD3loCD69+ cells.
claims.source: Despite the fact that roughly half of the purified CD4SP SM cells expressed CCR7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C), which is considered to be a hallmark of thymocyte medullary entry, accumulation of these cells within the medulla did not further increase, but instead remained at a twofold medullary: cortical density ratio, comparable to that of DPCD3loCD69+ cells (Figure 5A, B; Video 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 5A, B and Video 6.

claims.claim: Medullary accumulation of CD4SP SM cells was significantly reduced by CCR4 deficiency, regardless of the Ccr7 genotype.
claims.source: Medullary accumulation of this subset was significantly reduced by CCR4 deficiency, regardless of the Ccr7 genotype (Figure 5B, C), indicating an important role for CCR4 in promoting medullary localization of CD4SP SM cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 5B, C.

claims.claim: Paired analysis of Ccr7−/− versus WT CD4SP SM cells imaged together in the same slices showed that CCR7 also contributes to medullary accumulation of CD4SP SM cells.
claims.source: In addition, paired analysis of Ccr7−/− versus WT CD4SP SM cells imaged together in the same slices showed that CCR7 also contributes to medullary accumulation of CD4SP SM cells (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by paired analysis of two-photon imaging data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: CCR4 and CCR7 cooperate to promote medullary accumulation of CD4SP SM thymocytes.

results.result: CCR4 is upregulated within hours of positive selection, while CCR7 expression is delayed by 48-72 hours. Using synchronized positive selection assays with OT-II and OT-I TCR transgenic thymocytes on thymic slices, the authors show that CCR4 is upregulated as early as 3 hours after positive selection and continues to increase over 24 hours, while CCR7 is not detected until 48-72 hours post-positive selection.
results.evaluation: The temporal kinetics of CCR4 and CCR7 upregulation are well-supported by synchronized positive selection assays using both MHC-I and MHC-II restricted TCR transgenic systems (C73-C76, C80-C81). The data show consistent timing across both OT-I and OT-II models, with appropriate positive and negative controls (selecting vs. non-selecting slices). The conclusion that CCR4 upregulation precedes CCR7 by approximately 2 days is directly supported by the experimental data.

results.result: Thymocytes enter the medulla 9-12 hours after positive selection, coinciding with CCR4 upregulation but preceding CCR7 expression. Two-photon imaging of synchronized positive selection assays shows significant increases in medullary density of both OT-II and OT-I thymocytes by 9-12 hours after positive selection.
results.evaluation: The timing of medullary entry is well-documented by two-photon imaging data (C77, C82) showing significant increases in medullary density at 9-12 hours. The inference that CCR4 drives this early medullary entry (C78) is reasonable given the temporal correlation with CCR4 upregulation and the absence of CCR7 expression at this time point, though this remains correlative rather than mechanistic proof.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 show distinct expression patterns across post-positive selection thymocyte subsets. CCR4 is expressed by the majority of early DP CD3loCD69+ cells (which lack CCR7), persists on CD4SP SM cells (where ~40% also express CCR7), and is progressively downregulated in more mature subsets. CCR7 expression peaks in CD4SP and CD8SP M1 subsets and diminishes in M2 cells.
results.evaluation: The expression patterns are well-documented by flow cytometry data across multiple thymocyte subsets (C52-C56). The data clearly show the temporal progression of receptor expression, with appropriate controls including Ccr7-/- mice to distinguish true CCR7 expression from background. The quantification of percentages expressing each receptor provides robust support for the distinct expression patterns.

results.result: Early post-positive selection thymocytes respond to CCR4 but not CCR7 ligands, while mature thymocytes show robust CCR7-mediated chemotaxis. DP CD3loCD69+ cells undergo chemotaxis to CCL22 (CCR4 ligand) but not to CCL19 or CCL21 (CCR7 ligands). CD4SP SM cells show moderate responses to both CCR4 and CCR7 ligands. Mature CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 cells show highly efficient chemotaxis to CCR7 ligands and lose responsiveness to CCR4 ligands.
results.evaluation: The chemotaxis data (C58-C62, C65-C67) provide strong functional evidence for the differential receptor activity across developmental stages. The transwell assays include appropriate controls (blank wells), multiple chemokine concentrations, and statistical analysis. The functional data align well with the expression patterns, though the moderate CCR7-mediated chemotaxis of CD4SP SM cells only reaching significance when analyzed separately (C61) suggests this response is relatively weak.

results.result: CCR4 is required for medullary accumulation of early post-positive selection DP CD3loCD69+ thymocytes. Two-photon imaging shows WT DP CD3loCD69+ cells accumulate at twofold higher density in the medulla compared to cortex, and this medullary enrichment is abolished in Ccr4-/- and DKO mice but not affected by Ccr7 deficiency.
results.evaluation: The imaging data (C86-C88) provide strong evidence for CCR4's role in early medullary accumulation. The use of paired analyses comparing cells of different genotypes imaged simultaneously in the same slices (C88) is a rigorous approach that controls for slice-to-slice variability. The genetic specificity (loss of medullary enrichment in Ccr4-/- but not Ccr7-/- cells) strongly supports the conclusion.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 cooperate to promote medullary accumulation of CD4SP SM thymocytes. Despite ~50% of CD4SP SM cells expressing CCR7, their medullary:cortical density ratio remains at twofold (similar to DP CD3loCD69+ cells). Both CCR4 and CCR7 deficiency reduce medullary accumulation of this subset.
results.evaluation: The imaging data (C90-C92) demonstrate that both receptors contribute to medullary accumulation of CD4SP SM cells, with paired analyses showing significant effects of both Ccr4 and Ccr7 deficiency. The observation that CCR7 expression alone does not increase medullary accumulation beyond that of CCR7- DP cells (C90) is a key finding that challenges the prevailing model. The cooperative role is well-supported by the genetic data.

results.result: CCR7 is required for robust medullary accumulation of mature CD4SP M1+M2 thymocytes. These cells accumulate with a 4-5 fold medullary:cortical density ratio, and this accumulation is highly dependent on CCR7 but not significantly affected by CCR4 deficiency.
results.evaluation: The imaging data (C94-C96) clearly show that mature CD4SP cells achieve much higher medullary enrichment than earlier subsets, and this is CCR7-dependent. The lack of effect of CCR4 deficiency is consistent with the loss of CCR4 expression and responsiveness in M2 cells. The data support a developmental progression where CCR7 becomes the dominant driver of medullary localization in mature cells.

results.result: CCR7 expression is not synonymous with medullary localization. CCR7- DP CD3loCD69+ cells enter and accumulate in the medulla in a CCR4-dependent manner, while CCR7+ CD4SP SM cells do not show enhanced medullary accumulation compared to CCR7- DP cells. This challenges the prevailing model that equates CCR7 expression with medullary localization.
results.evaluation: This is a major conceptual finding well-supported by the imaging data showing CCR7- cells in the medulla (C102, C165) and CCR7+ cells not showing enhanced medullary enrichment (C103, C166). The conclusion that CCR7 expression cannot be used as a reliable surrogate for medullary localization (C164, C172) is justified by the data, though it's important to note this applies specifically to early post-positive selection stages and not to mature thymocytes.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 are required for early and late phases of negative selection, respectively. The majority of thymocytes undergoing negative selection express CCR4 but not CCR7. CCR4 deficiency reduces early-phase (DP) negative selection, while CCR7 deficiency reduces late-phase (CD4SP/CD8SP) negative selection. Double deficiency diminishes both phases.
results.evaluation: The cleaved caspase-3 data (C110-C116) provide strong evidence for differential roles of CCR4 and CCR7 in negative selection. The observation that most negatively selecting cells express CCR4 but not CCR7 (C110-C111) is important and well-documented. The genetic analysis showing phase-specific defects in single knockouts and combined defects in double knockouts (C114-C116) provides compelling evidence for non-redundant roles. The conclusion is well-supported by the data.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 collaboratively maintain self-tolerance in the colon. DKO mice show severe colonic inflammation with ulcerations, while Ccr4-/- mice show mild inflammation and Ccr7-/- mice show no colon inflammation. Histologic scores are significantly higher in DKO mice compared to WT.
results.evaluation: The histological data (C122-C126) clearly demonstrate differential autoimmune phenotypes across genotypes, with the most severe phenotype in DKO mice. The pathologist-blinded scoring adds rigor. The inference that CCR4 and CCR7 collaboratively maintain tolerance in the colon (C127) is supported by the synergistic effect in DKO mice, though the mechanism remains unclear. The autoantibody data (C121) provides additional evidence for systemic autoimmunity.

results.result: CCR7 plays a dominant role in promoting tolerance to endocrine organs. Immune infiltrates in liver, lacrimal glands, and submandibular glands are elevated in Ccr7-/- and DKO mice but not Ccr4-/- mice. This is consistent with CCR7's established role in mediating negative selection to TRAs expressed by mTECs.
results.evaluation: The histological data (C128) clearly show CCR7-dependent infiltrates in endocrine organs, with appropriate quantification. The conclusion that CCR7 plays a dominant role (C129) is well-supported by the selective phenotype in Ccr7-/- mice. The connection to TRA tolerance (C186) is supported by both the current data and cited literature, providing a mechanistic framework.

results.result: CCR4 maintains T cell homeostasis in secondary lymphoid organs. 70-75% of Ccr4-/- mice display moderate lymphoid hyperplasia in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes, with abnormal CD4 and CD8 distributions in T cell zones.
results.evaluation: The histological and immunofluorescence data (C130-C131, C188) document lymphoid hyperplasia specifically in Ccr4-/- mice. The phenotype is distinct from the endocrine organ infiltrates seen in Ccr7-/- mice, suggesting different mechanisms of tolerance failure. The conclusion about T cell homeostasis (C132) is reasonable given the data, though the underlying mechanism is not fully elucidated.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 ligands are expressed by distinct thymic APC subsets. CCR4 ligands (CCL17 and CCL22) are expressed by Sirpα+ cDC2 cells, activated CCR7+ cDCs, and thymic B cells. CCR7 ligands (CCL19 and CCL21) are expressed by mTEC subsets, with highest CCL21 expression by mTEClo cells.
results.evaluation: The qRT-PCR data (C133-C136, C183-C184) clearly demonstrate differential expression of CCR4 and CCR7 ligands by distinct APC subsets. The normalization to previously characterized high-expressing subsets is appropriate. The data provide a cellular basis for understanding how CCR4 and CCR7 might direct thymocytes to interact with different APCs, supporting the mechanistic model.

results.result: CCR4 promotes central tolerance to self-antigens expressed by LPS-activated APCs. LPS-stimulated splenocytes induce more proliferation of Ccr4-/- versus WT CD4+ T cells, while unstimulated or other TLR ligand-activated splenocytes do not show this differential effect.
results.evaluation: The T cell proliferation assay data (C141-C142, C189) provide functional evidence that Ccr4-/- T cells are less tolerant to antigens presented by LPS-activated APCs. The specificity for LPS (versus other TLR ligands) is important and well-documented. The conclusion that CCR4 promotes tolerance to activated APC antigens (C143) is supported by the data, though the mechanism (whether through thymic or peripheral tolerance) requires further investigation. The connection to CCR4 ligand expression by activated APCs strengthens the interpretation.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 may promote thymocyte interactions with distinct APC subsets. CCR4 may promote interactions with B cells and cDCs (including activated CCR7+ cDCs), while CCR7 may promote interactions primarily with mTECs. This could explain why CCR7 is particularly required for negative selection to TRAs.
results.evaluation: These claims (C137-C138, C185, C187) are presented as inferences and possibilities rather than demonstrated facts. While the ligand expression data and autoimmunity phenotypes are consistent with this model, direct evidence of differential APC interactions is not provided. The model is plausible and well-reasoned based on the available data, but would require additional experiments (such as imaging thymocyte-APC interactions or APC-specific ligand deletions) to be definitively supported.

results.result: CXCR4 expression and activity are compatible with medullary localization. All post-positive selection subsets except CD4SP SM and DP CD3+CD69+ cells undergo chemotaxis to CXCL12. Higher CXCR4 expression and responsiveness are observed in mature CD4SP and CD8SP M1 and M2 cells, which accumulate most in the medulla.
results.evaluation: The CXCR4 expression and chemotaxis data (C64, C178-C179) clearly show that CXCR4 activity is not incompatible with medullary localization, challenging a previous model. The observation of a developmental stage (CD4SP SM) where CXCR4 expression is uncoupled from function (C179-C180) is interesting and well-documented. The inference of a thymocyte-intrinsic mechanism (C180) is reasonable but speculative without additional mechanistic data.

results.result: CCR4 and CCR7 affect thymocyte migration properties. CCR7 deficiency reduces the speed of CD4SP M1+M2 cells, while double deficiency of Ccr4 and Ccr7 increases path straightness of all imaged subsets, suggesting that thymocytes responding to CCR4 and CCR7 ligands migrate in a more tortuous path.
results.evaluation: The track analysis data (C97-C99) from two-photon imaging provide quantitative evidence for effects on migration properties. The effect of CCR7 on speed (C98) is consistent with previous work. The increased straightness in DKO cells (C99) is an interesting observation, though the inference about tortuous migration (C100) is somewhat speculative. The data support the conclusion that these receptors affect migration behavior beyond just localization.

results.result: The study validates thymocyte subset definitions using Rag2p-GFP and Nr4a1GFP reporter mice. DP CD3loCD69+ cells represent post-positive selection thymocytes (not cells undergoing strong negative selection), and DP CD3+CD69+ cells represent MHC-I-restricted co-receptor reversing thymocytes.
results.evaluation: The validation of thymocyte subsets (C45-C51) using multiple reporter systems and MHC-deficient mice provides important methodological rigor. The Nr4a1GFP data (C47-C48) help distinguish post-positive selection from negatively selecting cells. The analysis in B2m-/- and MHCII-/- mice (C50-C51) provides strong evidence for the identity of DP CD3+CD69+ cells. This careful subset definition is critical for interpreting the subsequent experiments.

results.result: Thymocyte subset frequencies and CD5 expression levels are comparable between WT and Ccr4-/- mice, indicating that CCR4 deficiency does not grossly alter thymocyte development or selection stringency.
results.evaluation: The flow cytometry data (C106-C107) show no major differences in subset frequencies or CD5 levels (a proxy for self-reactivity) between WT and Ccr4-/- mice. This is important for establishing that the observed effects on negative selection and autoimmunity are not due to gross developmental defects. The data support the conclusion that CCR4's role is more subtle and specific.

results.result: CCL22 is expressed predominantly in the medulla, consistent with a potential role in inducing medullary entry of early post-positive selection thymocytes.
results.evaluation: The immunofluorescence data (C71) clearly show medullary localization of CCL22. This spatial distribution is consistent with CCR4's role in promoting medullary entry of early post-positive selection thymocytes. However, the claim notes this is "consistent with" rather than proving a causal role, which is appropriate given the correlative nature of the data.

results.result: Increased expression of cell-surface CCR7 or CCR4 was not detected with increasing incubation time at 37°C, ruling out that receptor internalization obscured detection of CCR7 or CCR4 on ex vivo thymocyte subsets.
results.evaluation: The control experiment (C57) addresses a potential technical concern about receptor internalization affecting the observed expression patterns. The data show no increase in surface expression with incubation time, supporting the conclusion that the measured expression levels reflect true differences rather than artifacts of receptor internalization. This is an important methodological control.

results.result: CD4SP SM cells respond efficiently to CCR4 ligands and undergo chemotaxis to CCL25 at levels comparable to DP CD3loCD69+ cells, demonstrating that these cells are not intrinsically unable to respond to chemokine receptor signaling despite their lack of strong CCR7 and CXCR4 responses.
results.evaluation: The chemotaxis data (C68-C69) demonstrate that CD4SP SM cells retain the ability to respond to some chemokine receptors (CCR4 and CCR9) even though they show weak responses to CCR7 and CXCR4. This is important for ruling out a general defect in chemokine responsiveness and supports the conclusion that receptor-specific regulatory mechanisms exist at this developmental stage.
